userPrompt: Oh, you should be able to read source spec as well.
systemPrompt:
We're working in a project whose spec is compiled to .claude/reference, which is where to read it. Each prompt starts with a <task-instructions> block saying what that prompt is for and what it may change. Follow the block at the top of the prompt you are answering; an earlier prompt's block no longer applies.

Its code is located in ./src.

Read the spec from its compiled reference under .claude/reference, where inheritance, expressions, and links are already resolved, or, for one thing, from what `piton slice` prints for it with this harness's adapter.

Before executing anything, read the spec it touches. Links to .claude/reference/... in the prompt are the spec for what they name. Read each one you need before changing anything it covers. Don't re-read something you've already read.
instructions:
We're only asking a question about the project. Answer it without changing anything.

The code is located in ./src.

harness-integration/index.md:17:Spec tasks, a Chain prompt's spec steps, and questions run the harness in a container the application owns, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says, which holds only what their mode may use; Code tasks and a Chain prompt's code step do too while the project's "Run code tasks in a container" option is on. Every other run, Code while the option is off, Freeform, and the application's own, runs the harness on the host, in the project directory. Either way the harness is run, prompted, and read just as this says.
harness-integration/index.md:21:The harness in use is the one picked in the [SettingsWindowScope](../settings-window/index.md#settings-window-scope): Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, Claude Code until another is picked. It is remembered for the user, as the [UserPreferencesScope](../user-preferences/index.md#user-preferences-scope) says, not for a project. Every run the application starts goes to it, the tasks, the questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the notes, commit messages, and prompt titles it writes, and everything else works the same whichever it is. A run already going when another is picked finishes with the harness it started with, and a conversation is only carried on by the harness it began with; the next request with another harness starts a new one.
harness-integration/index.md-22-Each harness is run its own way, streaming what it does as a line of JSON per event, which is read into the same reply, tool calls, usage, and result, whichever harness wrote it:
harness-integration/index.md-25-- Codex is `codex exec`, with `--full-auto` and `--json`, the prompt read from its standard input, a conversation carried on with `resume`.
harness-integration/index.md:28:Codex and OpenCode take no system prompt of their own, so it is given ahead of the prompt, marked off from it. Neither can carry on a copy of a conversation, so a question asked while another is running starts a new conversation with them instead. The notes, commit messages, and prompt titles are written with a small model where the harness can be told one, Claude Code's haiku, and with the harness's default model otherwise.
harness-integration/index.md-33-Only a run on the host has protected locations. A run in a container has none, since nothing it mustn't touch is mounted there, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says: it isn't guarded, and its harness is given no rule against reading or editing anything.
harness-integration/index.md:34:Where the harness takes rules for what its tools may do, as Claude Code does with `--disallowedTools`, a run on the host is told what its mode keeps it off. A Code task is told it may not edit the spec location, and a Spec task the code location; the application puts back whatever changes there all the same, and says so in the task's output as a passive notice, never an error, as the [TaskTableScope](../../ui/components/task-table/index.md#task-table-scope) says. A Code task and a question from the Ask tab are also told they may not read the spec location, alongside that, so they read the compiled reference instead, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says. This rule is only a nudge, and doesn't enforce anything, since a shell command can still read the files, and nothing puts anything back or stops the run when one does. A harness that takes no such rules is told nothing of either.
harness-integration/index.md-42-Codex's `codex exec` and OpenCode's `opencode run` read a single prompt and can't be fed more while they work, so a task running with either takes its prompt as ever and can't be sent more.
harness-integration/index.md:43:Questions, the palette's file search, the one-off runs, and the notes, commit messages, and prompt titles each take a single prompt, as ever.
harness-integration/index.md:47:Images attached to a prompt, as the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, are given to the harness as it takes them: to Claude Code as image content blocks, base64-encoded with their media type, in the same stream-json user message as the prompt's text, after it; to Codex with an `--image` argument per image; and to OpenCode with a `--file` argument per image. A message fed to a running Claude Code task carries its images the same way, and a Claude Code run that isn't fed more but has images is given its prompt as a stream-json message too, so the images can go with it. Codex's options end with `--` before the prompt when it is given images. Questions take images as tasks do.
harness-integration/index.md-51-The harness keeps its context between requests instead of starting fresh each time. Each lane of the [PromptSendingScope](../prompt-mode/sending/index.md#prompt-sending-scope) carries on a conversation of its own, so nothing a task of one lane read reaches a task of the other: the spec lane's, carried on by Spec tasks and a Chain prompt's spec steps, and the code lane's, carried on by Code tasks, a Chain prompt's code step, and Freeform tasks. Each task sent carries on its own lane's, and since a lane runs one task at a time, two tasks never carry on the same conversation at once. A Chain prompt's steps hand on to each other as text, the prompt and what the step before replied, as the [ModeSystemPromptsScope](../prompt-mode/mode-system-prompts/index.md#mode-system-prompts-scope) says, so the handoff crosses lanes whatever each lane's conversation holds. When the project is opened, each lane carries on the latest conversation among its own tasks in the history, a Chain task by the lane of the step it was.
harness-integration/index.md:53:Questions from the Ask tab share a separate conversation of their own, and when the project is opened they carry on the latest conversation among the questions saved with it. A question asked while another is running carries on a copy of that conversation, so questions running at the same time never write over each other. A conversation is only carried on in the project it began in, each open project keeping its own tasks' and questions' conversations while it is in the background. Questions run in a container, so a question carries on only a conversation begun in the questions' volume, never one saved from a question asked on the host before questions ran in containers, nor one whose session that volume no longer holds.
harness-integration/index.md:54:A request whose conversation can't be carried on, because the harness says it has no such session, as Claude Code's "No conversation found", or because it was begun elsewhere, is never failed for it, and never retried on the same conversation: it is sent again at once as a new conversation, the same prompt, with no context, and the conversation it couldn't carry on is not tried again by any later request, the project's history included. A question sent again so is recorded and shown as starting a new conversation, as the [AskConversationScope](../prompt-mode/ask-conversation/index.md#ask-conversation-scope) marks one. Each run applies its own prompt's systemPrompt, even when it carries on a conversation begun in a different mode. The palette's file search always starts fresh.
harness-integration/index.md:55:A conversation can be left for a new one, from the chat input's New conversation button, as the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) says, which leaves the conversation of the lane it is used for: the next request in it starts a new conversation with no context, and the one left is not carried on again, not by a run of it still going, nor by the project's history. Leaving it is kept with the project, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says, so a project opened after a lane's or the questions' conversation was left starts a new one there too, rather than carrying on the latest conversation in its history, until a run after the reset begins one of its own. How much context a conversation holds is known from what the harness reports with each reply: everything the model was given, cached or not, and what it wrote, as of its latest reply; replies of subagents don't count.
harness-integration/index.md:65:streamed, and where it gave none, what it printed on its standard error, and its exit status, as written. A task shows it in its output and a question at the end of its answer. It never reads only "the harness reported an error", or any other message that leaves the cause unnamed; a generic line is only ever a heading above what the harness said. A run that couldn't be started says why it couldn't, and one Podman couldn't run says so, as the [ContainerEnvironmentScope](../container-environment/index.md#container-environment-scope) says.

toolu_01XVsJpdG6iKKGNbAhKwRw4y.description: Check container spec for question mounts

content.content:
13:Spec tasks, a Chain prompt's spec steps, and questions from the Ask tab always run in a container. Code tasks and a Chain prompt's code step run in one only while the project's "Run code tasks in a container" option is on, as the [ProjectDataScope](../project-data/index.md#project-data-scope) says; while it is off, they run on the host as ever, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, with its protected locations. Freeform tasks always run on the host, and so do the application's own runs, the one-off runs, the palette's file search, and the notes, commit messages, and prompt titles, which change nothing.
14:Whatever runs in a container, the application itself still works on the host: it builds the spec before a task, takes the task's snapshots and lists the files it changed, shows diffs, and makes commits there, as ever.
23:Where `podman` isn't installed, a prompt that has to run in a container isn't sent, and never runs on the host instead: a Spec task, a Chain prompt's steps, a question, and, while the project's option is on, a Code task. It fails as a run whose harness isn't installed does, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says, or as one whose spec build can't run piton does, its output saying that Podman is needed to run it, with a link, opened in the browser when clicked, to Podman's installation instructions for the platform it is running on:
29:While the project's option is off, a Code task never needs Podman, and runs whether it is installed or not.
33:On macOS and Windows, a run also needs a Podman machine that is running. Where there is none, the task or question says so, and offers to set one up, a button reading "Set up Podman" that runs `podman machine init` and then `podman machine start`. Where there is one that isn't running, it says that, and offers to start it, a button reading "Start Podman" that runs `podman machine start`. Either shows what the command prints in the task's raw output as it runs, and once it succeeds, the prompt is sent again, as resending it would; one that fails says why, as a failed run does. On Linux there is no machine, and nothing about one is shown.
37:Where `podman` is installed, and on macOS and Windows its machine is running, but the application can't get Podman to run a container for it, as where the user may not use it, its rootless setup is missing, as the user's subordinate IDs, or it can't reach its service or machine, the run fails because of Podman, never because of the harness: it never reads "the harness reported an error", or any message that blames the harness or leaves the cause unnamed. The application tells this apart from a harness that ran and failed by what Podman itself reports, its exit status and what it prints before the harness starts in the container. The task's or question's output says plainly that the harness couldn't be run because Podman couldn't be accessed, and then gives, as written, what Podman printed about why. It is never run on the host instead. The same holds for a `podman build` of its image that fails for that reason: it says Podman couldn't be accessed, not only that the build failed.
43:While an image is being built for a run, the task or question shows "Preparing environment" as its status, and what the build prints goes to its raw output. A build that fails fails the run, saying why.
51:A Spec task, or a Chain prompt's spec step or spec follow-up: the spec location, read and write; the compiled reference, the harness directory's reference folder, read and write, so it can run `piton build` itself; the fluency file, read only; piton.config.pi, read only; and the task's understanding file, read and write. Never the code location.
53:##### Question
55:A question from the Ask tab: the code location, the compiled reference, and piton.config.pi, each read only. Never the spec location. Nothing is writable but the harness's own volumes.
59:A Code task, or a Chain prompt's code step, while the project's option is on: the code location, read and write; the compiled reference and piton.config.pi, read only; the task's understanding file, read and write; and the project's caches. Never the spec location.
62:A task's understanding file is mounted on its own, never the history folder it is in, so a run sees no other task's record. Since a file has to be there to be mounted, the application writes it empty just before the run, and an empty understanding file is shown as one not written yet is.
66:Where a mount can't be at the host's path, as on macOS and Windows, where the container sees the project at a path of its own, every path a run reports from its container is mapped back to its host path before it is shown or opened anywhere: the referenced spec in the right sidebar, file links in the task's output, its understanding file, the files it changed, and what its tool calls touched. A path that maps to nothing on the host is shown as the run gave it, and opens nothing.
73:- one per project and conversation, the spec lane's, the code lane's, and the questions', for the harness's sessions, so each carries on its own conversation, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says
74:- the project's caches, such as the cargo registry and target directory, for its Code tasks run in a container
80:When the harness isn't logged in, in its volume, the application runs its login command in a container, under a pseudo-terminal, and shows a login view in an inset panel, titled for the harness, with what the command prints. Any login URL the command prints opens in the host's browser. Where the command asks for a code to be pasted, the view has a field for it, and what is entered there goes to the command. Where the command waits for a callback on a known localhost port, that port is published for the login run. Where it offers to log in with a device code, that is how it logs in. The run waiting on the login is sent once the login succeeds, and fails, saying so, if it is cancelled or fails.
89:A Spec run can run `piton build` in its container, to check its work in the refreshed reference; with no code location there, what that build writes into the code location, the shape's guidance, goes nowhere. Once a Spec task or a Chain prompt's spec step is over, however it ended, the application runs `piton build` on the host, as the [SpecBuildScope](../spec-build/index.md#spec-build-scope) says, so the host's reference and shape guidance are those of the spec as the run left it.

59:A Code task, or a Chain prompt's code step, while the project's option is on: the code location, read and write; the compiled reference and piton.config.pi, read only; the task's understanding file, read and write; and the project's caches. Never the spec location.
62:A task's understanding file is mounted on its own, never the history folder it is in, so a run sees no other task's record. Since a file has to be there to be mounted, the application writes it empty just before the run, and an empty understanding file is shown as one not written yet is.
66:Where a mount can't be at the host's path, as on macOS and Windows, where the container sees the project at a path of its own, every path a run reports from its container is mapped back to its host path before it is shown or opened anywhere: the referenced spec in the right sidebar, file links in the task's output, its understanding file, the files it changed, and what its tool calls touched. A path that maps to nothing on the host is shown as the run gave it, and opens nothing.
73:- one per project and conversation, the spec lane's, the code lane's, and the questions', for the harness's sessions, so each carries on its own conversation, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says
74:- the project's caches, such as the cargo registry and target directory, for its Code tasks run in a container
80:When the harness isn't logged in, in its volume, the application runs its login command in a container, under a pseudo-terminal, and shows a login view in an inset panel, titled for the harness, with what the command prints. Any login URL the command prints opens in the host's browser. Where the command asks for a code to be pasted, the view has a field for it, and what is entered there goes to the command. Where the command waits for a callback on a known localhost port, that port is published for the login run. Where it offers to log in with a device code, that is how it logs in. The run waiting on the login is sent once the login succeeds, and fails, saying so, if it is cancelled or fails.
89:A Spec run can run `piton build` in its container, to check its work in the refreshed reference; with no code location there, what that build writes into the code location, the shape's guidance, goes nowhere. Once a Spec task or a Chain prompt's spec step is over, however it ended, the application runs `piton build` on the host, as the [SpecBuildScope](../spec-build/index.md#spec-build-scope) says, so the host's reference and shape guidance are those of the spec as the run left it.

I can't read the spec source from this run, and that matches the spec and the code as they're written now.

**What the spec says.** `.claude/reference/scope/container-environment/index.md:55`, under the Question heading:

> A question from the Ask tab: the code location, the compiled reference, and piton.config.pi, each read only. **Never the spec location.** Nothing is writable but the harness's own volumes.

Code tasks running in a container also never get the spec location (line 59). Spec tasks get the spec location but not the code (line 51). So in the current design no container run sees both the spec source and the code.

**What the code does.** `src/container.rs:179-183` (`RunKind::Question`) mounts exactly those three things, all read-only.

**What's actually in the container.** `piton.config.pi` sets `root: ./spec`, but `/home/hyphyphyph/piton/repl/spec` doesn't exist here. The only `.pi` file anywhere in the container is `piton.config.pi`. So `piton slice` wouldn't work either, even though the harness's instructions mention it.

**Your earlier question about `piton`.** The same spec page confirms what I said about where it runs. Line 14 says the application still builds the spec on the host before a task. Line 89 says that after a Spec task, the application runs `piton build` on the host. Only a Spec run may also run `piton build` inside its own container, to check its work.

If you want questions to see the spec source too, you'd change the Question entry in the ContainerEnvironmentScope. You'd add the spec location, read-only, and add `mounts.extend(spec.clone().map(ro))` to that branch in `container.rs`. Since this is a question-only prompt, I haven't changed anything.
